Summary: Core Platform Architecture & Multi-Outlet Foundation
Description: Establish foundational RESTful API, database schemas, seed configurations, and outlet domain models for campus food stalls.

Summary: Student Identity & Secure Campus Authentication
Description: Implement role-based JWT authentication separating student patrons from outlet staff with password hashing and session tokens.

Summary: Dynamic Food Chart & Outlet Browsing Experience
Description: Deliver interactive visual campus food chart with outlet cards, live operational status, operating hours, and categorized menu browsing.

Summary: Cart Management & Tamper-Proof Order Placement
Description: Build responsive shopping cart with single-outlet conflict prevention and server-side cryptographic price verification at checkout.

Summary: Real-Time Kitchen Display & Order Pipeline (KDS)
Description: Empower outlet kitchen staff with a dedicated KDS dashboard to track incoming tickets and transition order states smoothly.

Summary: Delivery Tracking, Voyage History & Production Hardening
Description: Provide student voyage order tracking, automated integration tests, runtime resilience fallbacks, and production security hardening.

Summary: Multi-Outlet Seed & Campus Data Model
Description:
As a platform administrator, I want to seed standardized Bennett University outlet metadata (IK, HC, SS, SN, HS) so that all menus, operating hours, and stall locations are consistently modeled.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given the database is initialized, when seed.js runs, 5 campus outlets must be populated with valid IDs, names, and menu items.
- Given existing records, seeding must perform an idempotent upsert without duplicating documents.
- Each outlet record must contain operational status (open/closed) and wait times.

Summary: Resilient In-Memory & Production MongoDB Connection Layer
Description:
As a backend engineer, I want a dual-mode database connection architecture that automatically boots an in-memory MongoDB instance if the external Atlas cluster is unreachable, so that local development and academic evaluation never fail.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given an unreachable MONGO_URI, when server boots, it catches the error and initializes MongoMemoryServer transparently.
- Seeding must execute automatically on fallback initialization.
- Application logs must clearly indicate whether Atlas or In-Memory storage is active.

Summary: Bennett University Student JWT Authentication
Description:
As a Bennett University student, I want to authenticate using my campus email and password so that I receive a secure JWT bearer token to access authorized food ordering features.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given valid student credentials (e.g. prikshit@bennett.edu.in), system returns a signed JWT containing student ID and role.
- Given invalid credentials, system returns HTTP 401 with informative error.
- Passwords must be hashed using bcrypt prior to database storage.

Summary: Outlet Staff Credential Verification & Role Isolation
Description:
As an outlet kitchen operator, I want to log in using my staff badge ID (e.g., IK-STAFF-001) so that I receive a staff-scoped JWT token restricting my view strictly to my stall's live kitchen orders.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given a staff badge and password, system validates credentials and embeds outletId into JWT payload.
- Staff token cannot access or manipulate orders belonging to other outlets.
- Staff token cannot place customer orders.

Summary: Interactive Campus Food Chart Outlet Discovery
Description:
As a student explorer, I want to view a visual nautical chart of campus dining stalls with real-time operational badges and estimated preparation times so that I can decide where to eat.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given the student dashboard loads, cards for Kathi Castle, Southern Soul, Chai & More, etc. render dynamically.
- Outlets display live Open/Closed status, operating hours, and average wait time.
- Clicking an outlet triggers the detailed menu modal.

Summary: Categorized Outlet Menu Modal & Item Browsing
Description:
As a hungry patron, I want to browse items within an outlet categorized into Beverages, Quick Bites, and Meals with prices and dietary badges (Veg/Non-Veg) so that I can easily select items.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given an outlet is selected, modal displays all active menu items grouped by category.
- Each item displays thumbnail, name, description, price in INR, and dietary indicator.
- Add to Cart button increases item count with immediate visual feedback.

Summary: LocalStorage Persistent Cart & Cross-Outlet Conflict Prevention
Description:
As a student ordering food, I want my cart to persist across page refreshes and prevent mixing items from different outlets so that kitchen dispatch remains clean and manageable.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Cart state persists in localStorage across browser reloads.
- Attempting to add an item from Outlet B while Cart contains items from Outlet A prompts clear-cart confirmation modal.
- Increment, decrement, and item removal dynamically update subtotal, tax, and order total.

Summary: Cryptographically Verified Server-Side Order Checkout
Description:
As a security-conscious engineer, I want the backend to re-calculate item prices from database source-of-truth during checkout rather than trusting client-submitted prices, preventing client-side price tampering exploits.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given checkout payload with altered item prices (e.g. ₹1 instead of ₹180), backend ignores client price and fetches DB price.
- Backend verifies student JWT token and links order to student ID.
- Order record created with status 'incoming', unique Order ID (#101), and initial voyage log.

Summary: Real-Time Kitchen Display System (KDS) for Outlet Staff
Description:
As an outlet cook, I want a dedicated Kanban-style kitchen display showing active tickets organized by status so that my crew can prioritize food preparation during peak campus rush hours.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given staff logs into KDS, only tickets matching the authenticated staff outletId are rendered.
- Tickets display customer name, ordered items, quantity, special instructions, and elapsed timer.
- Visual alerts trigger for orders waiting longer than 15 minutes.
Sprint: THH Sprint 3 - Kitchen Display & Live Tracking

Summary: 4-Stage Order Pipeline State Machine Transitions
Description:
As kitchen staff, I want to advance order status sequentially through incoming -> preparing -> ready -> completed via secure API endpoints so that both staff and students stay synchronized.

Acceptance Criteria:
- PATCH /api/orders/:id/status endpoint enforces valid sequential state transitions.
- Disallowed state skips (e.g., incoming -> completed) return HTTP 400 Bad Request.
- Timestamps are recorded for each transition milestone.
Sprint: THH Sprint 3 - Kitchen Display & Live Tracking

Summary: Student Voyage Log & Live Order Status Polling
Description:
As a student waiting for lunch, I want a live Voyage Log displaying an animated compass timeline reflecting my order's current stage so that I know exactly when to walk to the outlet counter.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Student order tracking screen fetches order updates via polling/WebSocket.
- Active stage lights up on nautical milestone tracker (Docked -> Cooking -> Ready -> Picked Up).
- Notification badge sounds or alerts when order moves to 'ready'.
Sprint: THH Sprint 3 - Kitchen Display & Live Tracking

Summary: Port Conflict Resolution & Dynamic Local Environment Switching
Description:
As a DevOps engineer, I want the system to dynamically bind to port 5001 when macOS ControlCenter AirPlay occupies port 5000 and update frontend API baseUrl automatically, ensuring zero runtime initialization collisions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Environment variable PORT=5001 respected in backend config.
- Frontend script.js detects window.location or environment config to route API calls to active port.
- Health check endpoint GET /api/health responds with HTTP 200 and uptime metrics.
Sprint: THH Sprint 4 - Hardening, Quality & Production Release

Summary: End-to-End Integration Test Suite & Automated Verification
Description:
As a QA test engineer, I want an automated end-to-end integration test script that verifies student auth, outlet browsing, tamper-proof order creation, staff order transition, and voyage log delivery in a single pipeline run.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Test suite executes all 5 core stages against running backend.
- Exit code 0 returned on 100% test pass; non-zero on failure.
- Detailed assertions verify payload types, JWT claims, and price calculations.
Sprint: THH Sprint 4 - Hardening, Quality & Production Release

Summary: Production Hardening, CORS & Helmet Security Audit
Description:
As a security auditor, I want to sanitize HTTP headers, configure CORS domain whitelisting, and implement error masking so that no stack traces or MongoDB connection strings are exposed in API error payloads.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Helmet middleware attached to Express application.
- CORS configured with explicit allowed origins.
- Generic 500 Internal Server Error returned to clients with internal logging.
Sprint: THH Sprint 4 - Hardening, Quality & Production Release
